note: Referensi multi-sumber: WHO, jurnal peer-reviewed internasional (NEJM, Lancet, JAMA, MDPI, JMIR), dan Kemenkes RI.

items.title: Physical Activity (Fact Sheet)
items.quote: Adults should do at least 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic physical activity per week, or at least 75–150 minutes of vigorous-intensity activity, for substantial health benefits.

items.title: WHO Guidelines on Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour (2020)
items.quote: Physical inactivity is the fourth leading risk factor for global mortality. Reducing sedentary behaviour and increasing physical activity at all intensities provides health benefits.

items.title: Effect of physical inactivity on major non-communicable diseases worldwide: an analysis of burden of disease and life expectancy
items.publisher: The Lancet — Kohl HW et al.
items.quote: Physical inactivity causes 6–10% of the world's burden of coronary heart disease and type 2 diabetes. Eliminating inactivity would increase global life expectancy by 0.68 years.

items.title: How Many Steps/day are Enough? For Adults
items.publisher: Int. J. Behavioral Nutrition and Physical Activity — Tudor-Locke C et al.
items.quote: Taking 10,000 steps/day is a reasonable target for healthy adults. Cadence of ≥100 steps/min during at least 10 minutes reflects moderate-intensity walking.

items.title: 2011 Compendium of Physical Activities: A Second Update of Codes and MET Values
items.publisher: Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise — Ainsworth BE et al.
items.quote: The Compendium provides validated MET values for hundreds of physical activities. Walking at moderate pace = MET 3.8; vigorous running = MET 11.0.

items.title: Cara Menjaga Kesehatan Jantung dengan Aktivitas Fisik
items.quote: Berjalan cepat selama 30 menit setiap hari memberikan dukungan besar bagi kesehatan jantung dan menurunkan risiko penyakit tidak menular.

items.title: Tobacco (Fact Sheet)
items.quote: Tobacco kills up to half of its users. More than 8 million people die from tobacco use each year, including around 1.3 million non-smokers exposed to second-hand smoke.

items.title: Association of Smoking Cessation with Subsequent Risk of Cardiovascular Disease
items.quote: Smoking cessation was significantly associated with lower risks of cardiovascular disease. Benefits appeared within 5 years of quitting and improved progressively over time.

items.title: Cigarette Smoking and Telomere Length in Men and Women
items.publisher: Environmental Health Perspectives — Valdes AM et al.
items.quote: Smoking accelerates biological aging. Smokers had shorter telomeres equivalent to approximately 4.6 extra years of biological aging compared to non-smokers.

items.title: Kawasan Tanpa Rokok (KTR) — Pedoman Pelaksanaan
items.quote: Paparan asap rokok orang lain meningkatkan risiko penyakit jantung koroner sebesar 25–30% dan kanker paru sebesar 20–30%.

items.title: Guideline: Sugars Intake for Adults and Children
items.quote: Reduce free sugars to less than 10% of total energy intake. A further reduction below 5% (~25 g/day) would provide additional health benefits.

items.title: Sugar-Sweetened Beverages and Risk of Metabolic Syndrome and Type 2 Diabetes
items.publisher: Diabetes Care — Malik VS et al.
items.quote: Consumption of 1–2 servings/day of sugar-sweetened beverages is associated with a 26% greater risk of developing type 2 diabetes, independent of obesity.

items.title: Batasan Konsumsi Gula, Garam, dan Lemak
items.quote: Batas konsumsi gula per hari: 4 sendok makan (50 g). Kelebihan konsumsi gula meningkatkan risiko diabetes mellitus tipe 2 dan penyakit kardiovaskular.

items.title: A Healthy Lifestyle — WHO Recommendations
items.quote: A BMI ≥25 kg/m² (overweight) and ≥30 kg/m² (obesity) increases risk of cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, musculoskeletal disorders, and certain cancers.

items.title: Body-Mass Index and Mortality among 1.46 Million White Adults
items.publisher: New England Journal of Medicine — Berrington de Gonzalez A et al.
items.quote: The lowest mortality risk was at a BMI of 20.0–24.9 kg/m². Excess body weight was significantly associated with all-cause mortality across all demographic groups.

items.title: CERDIK, Rahasia Masa Muda Sehat dan Masa Tua Nikmat!
items.quote: CERDIK (Cek kesehatan, Enyahkan rokok, Rajin aktivitas, Diet sehat, Istirahat cukup, Kelola stres) adalah enam pilar pencegahan penyakit tidak menular sesuai pedoman Kemenkes RI.

items.title: Mental Health Atlas 2020
items.quote: Sleep disorders are closely associated with poor mental health and increased risk of chronic disease. Adults need 7–9 hours of adequate sleep per night for overall well-being.

items.title: Sleep Duration and Type 2 Diabetes: A Meta-Analysis of Prospective Studies
items.publisher: Diabetes Care — Shan Z et al.
items.quote: Both short sleep duration (≤6 hrs) and long sleep duration (≥9 hrs) are independently associated with elevated risk of type 2 diabetes. Short sleepers had a 37% increased risk.

items.title: Sleep and the Immune System
items.publisher: Physiological Reviews — Besedovsky L et al.
items.quote: Sleep is an active immunological process. Sleeping less than 6 hours significantly reduces vaccine efficacy by up to 50% and increases infection susceptibility.

items.title: Germas: Tidur Cukup untuk Kesehatan Optimal
items.quote: Orang dewasa membutuhkan 7–9 jam tidur berkualitas per malam. Kurang tidur meningkatkan risiko hipertensi, diabetes, dan gangguan imunitas.

items.title: World Mental Health Report: Transforming Mental Health for All
items.quote: Chronic stress activates physiological stress responses continuously, leading to systemic inflammation, accelerated aging, and increased risk of cardiovascular disease and depression.

items.title: Job Strain as a Risk Factor for Coronary Heart Disease
items.publisher: The Lancet — Kivimäki M et al. (IPD-Work Consortium)
items.quote: Work stress is associated with a 23% excess risk of heart attack. Chronic psychological stress promotes atherosclerosis through cortisol elevation and pro-inflammatory pathways.

items.title: Kesehatan Jiwa: Pedoman Nasional Pelayanan Kedokteran
items.quote: Pengelolaan stres melalui relaksasi, olahraga teratur, dan dukungan sosial terbukti mengurangi risiko gangguan jiwa dan penyakit tidak menular.

items.title: Diabetes (Fact Sheet)
items.quote: A healthy diet, regular physical activity, normal body weight, and avoiding tobacco use can prevent or delay the onset of type 2 diabetes.

items.title: 10-year follow-up of diabetes incidence in the Diabetes Prevention Program Outcomes Study
items.publisher: The Lancet — Knowler WC et al.
items.quote: Lifestyle intervention (diet + exercise) reduced diabetes incidence by 34% at 10-year follow-up, demonstrating durable benefits beyond the active intervention period.

items.title: Pedoman Pengendalian Diabetes Melitus
items.quote: Pencegahan diabetes melitus tipe 2 dapat dilakukan melalui pola makan sehat, aktivitas fisik minimal 150 menit/minggu, dan pemantauan gula darah secara berkala.

items.title: Pima Indians Diabetes Database (Dataset Description)
items.quote: Benchmark dataset widely used in diabetes risk classification research. Includes DiabetesPedigreeFunction as a validated genetic risk factor predictor.

items.title: Healthy Diet (Fact Sheet)
items.quote: Consume at least 1.5–2 liters of water per day (~8 glasses). Adequate hydration supports kidney function, digestion, thermoregulation, and cognitive performance.

items.title: Mild Dehydration Impairs Cognitive Performances and Mood of Men
items.publisher: British Journal of Nutrition — Masento NA et al.
items.quote: Even mild dehydration (1–2% body weight loss) impairs attention, short-term memory, and psychomotor processing speed in healthy adults.

items.title: Germas: Gaya Hidup Sehat Masyarakat Indonesia
items.quote: Minum air putih minimal 8 gelas per hari adalah salah satu dari tiga pilar utama Gerakan Masyarakat Hidup Sehat (GERMAS).

items.title: Panduan Isi Piringku
items.quote: Satu piring makan terdiri dari: ½ bagian sayur dan buah, ¼ bagian protein (ikan/ayam/tahu/tempe), ¼ bagian karbohidrat (nasi/ubi/jagung). Batasi gula, garam, dan lemak.

items.title: Health effects of dietary risks in 195 countries (GBD 2017 Diet Collaborators)
items.publisher: The Lancet — Afshin A et al.
items.quote: Poor diet is responsible for more deaths globally than any other risk factor, including tobacco. Suboptimal diet leads to 11 million preventable deaths per year worldwide.

items.title: Hypertension (Fact Sheet)
items.quote: Hypertension affects 1.28 billion adults worldwide. Reducing sodium intake, increasing physical activity, and limiting alcohol can prevent or control hypertension.

items.title: Puasa Aman bagi Penderita Hipertensi
items.quote: Penderita hipertensi perlu memperhatikan pola makan dan minum saat sahur dan berbuka agar puasa tetap aman dan tekanan darah terjaga.

items.title: Puasa Lancar, Badan Bugar: Berbuka Lebih Sehat
items.quote: Saat berbuka, pilih minum air putih dan batasi makanan/minuman manis berlebihan agar tubuh lebih bugar selama berpuasa.

items.title: Intermittent Fasting and Human Metabolic Health
items.publisher: Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics — Patterson RE et al.
items.quote: Intermittent fasting regimens may improve metabolic risk factors including triglycerides, LDL cholesterol, blood pressure, waist circumference, and systemic inflammatory markers.

items.title: Ultraviolet (UV) Radiation
items.quote: Excessive UV radiation damages DNA in skin cells, causing premature skin aging (photoaging), sunburn, and increased risk of skin cancer. SPF 30+ sunscreen reduces UV exposure by 97%.

items.title: Skin Aging — Review Article
items.quote: Skin aging results from intrinsic (genetic, telomere shortening) and extrinsic (UV exposure, smoking, pollution) factors. Oxidative stress plays a central role in accelerating both processes.

items.title: Gait as a Biomarker of Healthy Aging: A Systematic Review
items.quote: Gait variability (coefficient of variation of stride time) is a strong predictor of fall risk, cognitive decline, and frailty. Passive smartphone-based gait monitoring is a scalable screening approach.

items.title: Smartphone-Based Gait Analysis for the Detection of Frailty in Older Adults
items.publisher: JMIR mHealth and uHealth — Del Din S et al.
items.quote: Smartphone inertial sensors reliably detect gait quality features including cadence, step regularity, and asymmetry with accuracy comparable to laboratory-grade reference systems.

items.title: Human Activity Recognition Using Accelerometer and Gyroscope Sensors
items.publisher: MDPI Sensors — Lara OD, Labrador MA
items.quote: Accelerometer-based HAR achieves 92–97% accuracy using signal features such as mean, variance, spectral entropy, and zero-crossing rate with ensemble classifiers.

items.title: GPS and Inertial Sensor Fusion for Pedestrian Navigation Using Kalman Filter
items.publisher: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
items.quote: Kalman Filter-based GPS + accelerometer fusion significantly reduces positioning error in pedestrian tracking, particularly in urban environments with degraded GPS signals.
